claims.text: In as-deposited nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films and nanoribbons, magnetocaloric response and low-field hysteresis are primarily governed by interfacial magnetoelastic strain and nanoscale lattice distortion.
Interfacial strain and lattice distortion disrupt coherent ferromagnetic-domain formation in the nanostructures.
Coherent ferromagnetic-domain formation is typical of bulk FeMnNiGeSi material.
Disruption of coherent domains reduces magnetocaloric efficiency.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi nanostructures contain substantial intrinsic lattice distortions and strain-induced inhomogeneities.
A low-temperature inert-atmosphere anneal below the recrystallization threshold is the proposed controlled intervention.
Such annealing will relieve interfacial and grain-boundary strain without significant phase segregation or grain growth.
The annealing temperature should be well below 0.5 times the alloy melting temperature and the duration should be short enough to preserve nanoscale dimensions.
Magnetoelastic strain at interfaces and nanoscale grain boundaries mediates magnetic-domain formation and stability.
Interfacial and lattice strains produce disordered and spatially inhomogeneous magnetic exchange interactions.
The resulting non-uniform magnetic-domain structure enhances hysteresis.
Strain-induced exchange and domain inhomogeneity broadens the magnetocaloric transition.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation will produce more coherent and uniform magnetic-domain order.
Annealed specimens will have lower hysteresis-loop area and coercivity than as-deposited controls during low-field cooling cycles.
Annealed specimens will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change per unit applied field than as-deposited controls.
Annealed specimens will exhibit reduced heat-transfer lag relative to as-deposited controls.
The as-deposited baseline has a broadened, hysteretic magnetocaloric transition and diminished cooling-cycle performance.
The proposed operating regime uses applied magnetic fields below 100 mT.
Thermal-transfer rates in the proposed devices are limited by nanoscale geometry.

Failure of annealing to produce a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and enhanced entropy change together with more coherent domains would falsify the claim that interfacial magnetoelastic strain is dominant.
